title: fix(cli): `os data delete`'s human arm reads the server's `success` flag (#19413)
body:
Fixes #19413

Clause-②: no

`os data delete` renders three output faces from one call. The `--format json` and
`--format yaml` arms lower the server's `DeleteDataResponse.success` into their own
`deleted` key — that is what #5638 landed, and its note is still in the command. The
default human-readable arm did not read it at all: it printed `Record deleted: rec_1`
unconditionally. One command, one call, two output formats able to state opposite facts
about whether a row is gone.

## Re-derived premise — the card's line numbers, and then the order's

The card cites `:68-77`. Re-derived on the tree this branch forked from
(`origin/main` `576d5df660`), the numbers are the dispatch order's, exactly:

| what | line |
|---|---|
| `if (flags.format === 'json') {` | 69 |
| `deleted: result.success,` (json arm) | 74 |
| yaml arm, same `deleted: result.success` | 77 |
| `printSuccess(...Record deleted...)` — the defect | 79 |

## ⚠️ The premise moved under this branch: #19411 landed mid-task

The order records #19411 as open and still a draft, and says the contradiction is
therefore latent. It merged while this was being written (`f9e16d856b`, on `main`), and
this branch has merged `main` since. `MetadataProtocol.deleteData` used to return the
literal `success: true`; it now returns `success: deleted !== 0`, so a package-declared
`sys_permission_set` — whose delete is an ADR-0005 reset that re-projects the row rather
than removing it — answers `success: false` on the live door.

⇒ the contradiction is now **reachable on `main`**, not latent: from that commit on,
`os data delete sys_permission_set rec_1` printed `Record deleted` for a row the same
command's `--format json` arm reported as `deleted: false`. See Acceptance notes for the
triage consequence, which is not this PR's to write.

## What the order left open, and what the measurement settled

**Which carrier.** `printWarning` (`  ⚠ ...`), not `printError` (`  ✗ ...`): the command
ran and the server answered; `✗` reads as a failed run and would imply the non-zero exit
this deliberately does not take.

**The exit code does not move — on either arm, in any format.** The two machine arms
already publish `success: true`, the CLI envelope's *"the command completed"* flag,
beside `deleted: false`, and they exit `0`.

- Moving **only** the human arm off `0` would re-create this very defect one layer down:
  the same call exiting `0` under `--format json` and non-zero by default. That is the
  card's own shape, relocated from the sentence to the exit code.
- Moving it on **all three** arms would narrow a published CLI accept set — a script that
  succeeds today would start failing — which is a contract change, and this card carries
  no ruling for one.

⇒ exit `0` in both directions, and pinned in both directions so the next change cannot
move it silently. That is what makes this a `patch` rather than the `minor` + `**BREAKING**`
+ ADR-0087 shape the order names for the narrowing branch.

**The flag is read as `=== false`, not as falsiness** — the same reading
`MetadataProtocol.deleteData` takes of the driver contract, and the one #19411 reaffirmed
in its own note (*"only a POSITIVE zero is read as 'not removed'"*). An absent or
`undefined` flag from an off-contract server is no signal at all, and turning "no signal"
into "not deleted" would make this command deny deletions that really happened.

## The escape hatch was checked and does not apply

The order offers *"the human arm cannot read the flag without a change in
`@objectstack/client`'s return type"* as a legitimate outcome. Measured, it is false:

- `DeleteDataResult` already declares `success: boolean`, **required** — no widening needed.
- `unwrapResponse` strips an envelope only when the body carries **both** a boolean
  `success` **and** a `data` key, so the flat delete payload passes through verbatim.
- the `fetch` wrapper throws only on a non-2xx status, so a `200` carrying
  `success: false` reaches the command intact.

All three are asserted by the POSITIVE CONTROL case rather than left as prose, so if any
of them stops holding, that case reddens before the rest of the file can measure a fiction.

## Test — the package's first for this command

`packages/cli/src/commands/data/delete-arms-agree.test.ts`. There was no existing test
file for `data/delete.ts` (the only `delete*.test.ts` in the package sit under
`src/commands/meta/`, which are the harness precedents this follows). Six cases:

1. **POSITIVE CONTROL** — a `success: false` body reaches the command through the real
   SDK, and the `true` body arrives just as verbatim. Nothing imports from #19411.
2. **LIT CONTROL** — `success: true` still prints today's sentence, asserted as the
   **whole** output, byte for byte.
3. `success: false` — the human arm does not assert a deletion.
4. **All three arms state the same fact** for one and the same result, both ways round —
   the assertion the card is actually about.
5. The exit code is `0` on both arms across all three formats.
6. A genuine transport failure still exits `1` — the control for pin 5, so that `0` reads
   as a decision rather than as this command having lost the ability to fail.

Both sentences are pinned **whole**, not by substring: `Record deleted: rec_1` and
`Not deleted: rec_1 — the server reported the deletion did not happen` share the token
`deleted`, so a `toContain` pin would be satisfied by either.

## Reverse verification — run on the final tree, `3283cefddb`

Through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, so the mutation is proven on disk rather than
trusted to an editor's exit code. `if (result.success === false) {` replaced with
`if (false) {` — the pre-fix behaviour exactly:

```text
ablation-replace: anchor   x1 -> x0
ablation-replace: replace  "if (false) {"  x0 -> x1
ablation-replace: blob     160538b32cd2... -> ced8a46366b9...
ablation-replace: ok mutation landed: anchor 1 -> 0, blob 160538b32cd2 -> ced8a46366b9

  × `success: false` — the human arm does NOT assert a deletion
  × all three arms state the SAME fact, for one and the same result
  Tests  2 failed | 4 passed (6)

  AssertionError: expected [ false, false, true ] to deeply equal [ false, false, false ]

ablation-replace: ok restored: blob == HEAD (160538b32cd2) and `git diff HEAD` is empty
```

Direction observed: **turns red**, on exactly the two pins the guard is about — and the
lit control and both exit-code pins stayed green, so the ablation did not simply break
everything. Restore proven byte-identical to `HEAD`, not by an exit code.

## Evidence

| what | command | result |
|---|---|---|
| new pin, final tree | `vitest run --project unit ...delete-arms-agree.test.ts` | 6 passed |
| package unit tier | `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project unit` | 221 files / 3120 tests passed, exit 0 |
| package typecheck | `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck` | exit 0 (test layer compiles too) |
| dependency closure | `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/cli^...' build` | exit 0 |
| derived gate families | `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` | 61 derived, 61 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED |

`packages/cli`'s `integration` tier is declared to CI, not run locally: this diff touches
no spawn entry (`bin/`, `test/helpers/serve-process.ts`) and no driver or kernel boot
path, so the new file lands in `unit` by `packages/cli/vitest-tiers.ts`'s predicate.

Two families first answered `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (exit 3, *"nothing was measured"*)
because the worktree had no full `dist/`; both were re-run green after `pnpm build`, and
one more was killed by this runner's own 300s cap and re-run green with a real budget.
None of the three is recorded as a failed measurement.

## Changeset — the level was measured, not judged

`patch`, on `@objectstack/cli`. `skip-changeset` is refused by measurement: the package's
published `files[]` ships `dist`, and after a build the new sentence is present in
`dist/commands/data/delete.js`, with the unchanged success sentence from the same file as
the lit control and the new test file absent from `dist` entirely as the negative control.

Not `minor` + breaking: the exit code and the accept set are both unchanged, and the
`--format json` / `--format yaml` bytes are untouched in both directions.

## Acceptance notes

**Governance.** This diff touches no governed surface (Prime Directive #14) — only
`packages/cli/**` and one `.changeset/` entry.

**File surface.** Exactly the order's fence: `delete.ts` + one new sibling test + a
changeset. No fourth file was needed.

**For the triage seat, not for this PR.** The `os-sam` triage comment on the card states a
machine-checkable upgrade trigger: *"When objectstack-ai/objectstack#19411 merges,
re-grade this card `priority:p1` + `security`."* That merge has now happened. This PR
writes no labels and re-grades nothing — the trigger is recorded here so the seat that
owns grading sees it.

Out-of-scope observations, noted and not filed — neither is a defect, a contract breach or
an AI-metadata trap, so neither meets the three filing classes:

- noted, not filed: `packages/cli/test/remote-api-commands.test.ts` asserts only static
  oclif metadata (`description`, `args`, `flags`) for eleven commands including this one —
  no behaviour. It is why the package could carry a `data/delete` import and still have no
  behavioural pin. Observation about coverage shape, not a defect. Carrier: this PR is the
  one that adds the behavioural pin, so nothing is left hanging.
- noted, not filed: the `--format table` option is accepted by the flag declaration but
  reaches the same `else` arm as any unrecognised value, so `table` and the default render
  identically for this command. Pre-existing, unchanged here, and no author-facing metadata
  is dropped. Carrier: none — recorded only so the next reader of this arm does not read
  the `else` as table-specific.
